svg.text: AU Bank Insurance Distribution Platform — AWS platform request view (R0)
What the application is · the services it needs · which availability zone each one sits in · the DR estate in ap-south-2 · the reverse-proxy and egress chain · and WHEN each resource is needed
Rendering of docs/architecture/R0-LLD.md §2.1 (AZ placement) · §11.1 (DR bill of materials) · §12.1 (provisioning sequence) — owns nothing (HA-02)
HOW TO READ THIS — two colour axes, and they answer two different questions

CONTAINERS are coloured by WHERE: public AWS edge · VPC public subnet · VPC private-app · VPC private-data · DR region. SERVICE NODES are coloured by WHEN: build wave W0b→W4, or the workstream that already owns them (WS-1 exists today, WS-2 is workforce identity).

Solid = PROVISION in R0. Dashed grey = DO NOT PROVISION — it is in the target-state review and provisioning it now is scope drift. Nothing on this page may be built from the diagram alone: raise the request from R0-LLD.md §13.
WHAT KIND OF APPLICATION THIS IS
one assisted Term Life sale, end to end — not a portal, not a warehouse
A certified Bank Relationship Manager sells one Term Life policy to one existing bank customer, end to end, through a real insurer interface — with consent and
suitability evidence, payment taken on the customer's own device, an issued and reconciled policy, and a complete seven-year audit trail. Objective R0-ASSISTED-TERM-SALE.
It is a regulated transaction system, not a content or reporting system. It is correctness-, evidence- and recovery-constrained — NOT throughput-constrained.
AWS ORGANIZATIONS — FIVE ACCOUNTS, ONE VPC EACH
prod is a hard account boundary, not a namespace convention
ECR — the image is built ONCE here
synthetic data ONLY · single AZ, deliberately
Render.com preview allowed — never a data path
masked or synthetic · NO production CIF dumps
>= 2 AZs · the bank caller exercises quote + proposal
real ETB customers · pilot branches only

REGION PINNING IS A GUARDRAIL, NOT A CONVENTION — a Service Control Policy denies any region other than ap-south-1 and ap-south-2 before the first resource exists (S09-E01-S06, validated by S09-VT-02). Retro-fitting it means re-verifying every resource by hand for the S09-G9 residency attestation.
the customer's payment never enters our edge (C4)
opaque session cookie — never an OAuth token (S-01)
assist only · scoped to its own insurer_id
no platform session in R0 · not our VPC
R1 — do NOT provision a second
R2 actors on the SAME journey
no new edge, no new BFF
ap-south-1 (MUMBAI) · PRIMARY · ALL PRODUCTION DATA LIVES HERE
control C6 — no resource outside India, enforced by SCP and policy-as-code
PUBLIC AWS EDGE — NOT IN THE VPC · THE ONLY INTERNET ENTRY POINT
no workload is internet-reachable · no public ALB, no public RDS, no public EKS endpoint
NO latency-based DR routing in R0
DR failover is a manual, recorded act
no authN, no authZ, no business logic
IP-allowlisted to AU Bank PG only
VPC · ONE PER ENVIRONMENT · 10.{env}.0.0/16 · THREE AVAILABILITY ZONES
prod does not share a VPC with uat · no network path from a lower environment to production data (S09-E02-S03)

AVAILABILITY ZONES — pin AZ IDs (aps1-az1…), never AZ NAMES: a name maps to a different physical AZ in every account, so a name pinned across five accounts silently co-locates what was meant to be separated.
NAT and the Internet Gateway only. A public ALB or NLB onto a service is a standing-constraint violation.
dev: THIS ONE ONLY (single AZ, deliberate)
1SB and AU Bank PG allowlist this EIP
second EIP to publish for allowlisting
prod only — cost call with Shivanshi
PRIVATE-APP SUBNETS /20 per AZ · EKS worker nodes · internal ALB nodes · interface-endpoint ENIs
the /20 sizes POD IPs (VPC CNI), not node count — a /24 here is the mistake that caps the cluster
Worker nodes · ALB node · endpoint ENIs
uat/prod: >= 3 nodes. dev: this AZ only
Worker nodes · ALB node · endpoint ENIs
the second AZ is the FLOOR at which a PDB can drain
Worker nodes · ALB node · endpoint ENIs
removes 'lose an AZ, lose half the capacity'
AMAZON EKS · ONE PRIVATE CLUSTER PER ENVIRONMENT · workloads are SPREAD across the AZ columns above, not pinned to one
no PersistentVolumeClaim on any business service · no service mesh · EKS API endpoint private in prod
THE AZ RULE FOR EVERY SALE-PATH POD: minReplicas: 2 + topologySpreadConstraints over topology.kubernetes.io/zone + PodDisruptionBudget minAvailable: 1
two pods on one node in one AZ satisfies 'min 2' and survives nothing — the SPREAD is the control, not the replica count
Internal ALB — the ONLY reverse proxy inside the VPC (AWS Load Balancer Controller)
internal scheme · one ALB with host/path rules, NOT an ALB per microservice · a node in every enabled AZ · TLS re-terminated · no authN, no authZ · targets ns:edge only
the only namespace the internal ALB may target
#2 RM Workspace BFF (+ workforce-access-bff if packaged separately)
stateless session facade · holds the OAuth tokens so Flutter never does (S-01)
re-authorised by the PDP on every call (S-02) · aggregation only, no business rules
WS-2 · reachable from every app namespace on the PDP port only
Bank AD federation is WS-2 Phase 2
RBAC + ABAC · default deny · 300 ms budget
FAILS CLOSED — PDP down means nothing is authorised
never exposed to Flutter · >= 2 replicas, >= 2 AZs
JDBC to Aurora schema keycloak — NO PVC
LOB-agnostic and LOB-partitioned services — one deployment for every line of business
the hard gate before any quote
no Kafka — a table plus a worker
Health gets its OWN #10/#11 later — never an if (lob == …)
all provider traffic leaves through here (SC-W3-5)
exists today · mTLS via the NAT EIP
PRIVATE-DATA SUBNETS /24 per AZ · no 0.0.0.0/0 route — Aurora cannot initiate an outbound connection
no public RDS · no second cluster · ADR-008: ONE cluster, a schema per bounded context
16 schemas, separate owner role, no cross-schema GRANT
a writer is single-AZ by definition
MUST be in a DIFFERENT AZ from the writer — assert it in IaC
a reader in the writer's AZ is read-scaling, NOT availability
the single most common Multi-AZ misconfiguration
keeps the failover target open and costs nothing
ElastiCache would live here IF WS-2 sessions force it —
prefer DynamoDB sessions and provision none
VPC ENDPOINTS — one interface ENI per AZ for S3* · DynamoDB* · Secrets Manager · ECR (api + dkr) · STS · CloudWatch Logs (*S3 and DynamoDB are GATEWAY endpoints: attach to EVERY private route table)

An interface endpoint present in two of three AZs makes the third AZ's pods fail to pull images while every health check still reports green. A gateway endpoint missing from one route table sends that AZ's S3 traffic through NAT, quietly and billably.

EGRESS THAT DOES USE NAT: 1SilverBullet (HTTPS mTLS) · AU Bank PG session · CBS (once Direct Connect / VPN exists) · SMS / email gateway. East-west: Kubernetes NetworkPolicy default-deny per namespace, documented seams only.
AWS-MANAGED · REGIONAL — multi-AZ by construction, reached through the endpoints above. Do not build AZ logic around these.
CMK per class: data · logs · secrets · WORM
image built ONCE, promoted by digest
HOW MANY REVERSE PROXIES, WHERE, AND WHAT EACH ONE IS ALLOWED TO DO
two hops. Not three, not four.
R0 uses a TWO-HOP reverse proxy and there is no Nginx / Envoy sidecar estate behind it. Adding a fourth hop adds a PII and PCI surface with no R0 consumer.
EXTERNAL PROXY — the only public one
authN: no (an API key is not auth)
host / path routing to the BFF
DO WE NEED A THIRD-PARTY PROXY PRODUCT (Kong, Nginx Plus, F5)? No — not for R0. API Gateway + CloudFront + WAF IS the external reverse proxy, and the internal ALB IS the in-VPC one.

EGRESS PROXY: there is no forward-proxy product either. Outbound calls leave through the NAT Gateway on its fixed Elastic IP, which is what 1SB and the AU Bank PG allowlist. C4: the customer's payment never traverses this chain — the device goes straight to the AU Bank PG, and the callback returns on a separate, IP-allowlisted API Gateway route.
AVAILABILITY-ZONE PLACEMENT — WHICH RESOURCE SITS IN WHICH AZ
R0-LLD.md §2.1 · the sources said '3 AZs' and stopped; this is the placement contract
WHY THE NUMBER IS WHAT IT IS
Free to create, impossible to retrofit without renumbering
Interface VPC endpoints (Secrets, ECR, STS, Logs)
Two of three AZs = the third AZ fails to pull images, silently
Attach to EVERY private route table or that AZ pays NAT for S3
Subnets in all three; a node per enabled AZ
Losing it loses every RM session
Each EIP added is one more address 1SB and the PG must allowlist
uat: >= 3 nodes over >= 2 AZs · prod: 3 AZs
Two AZs is the floor at which PDB minAvailable:1 can still drain
The spread constraint is the control, not the replica count
The PDP fails closed — identity down is a total outage
One AZ at a time, by definition
Multi-AZ means the FAILOVER TARGET is elsewhere
A DIFFERENT AZ from the writer
Same-AZ reader = read scaling, not availability
DynamoDB · S3 · KMS · Secrets Manager · ECR
Nothing to place — do not build AZ logic around them
ElastiCache (ONLY if WS-2 sessions force it)
A single-node session store makes an AZ loss a mass logout

● required ◐ conditional (environment or a named decision) ○ deliberately absent — not AZ-bound Three AZs for anything free (subnets, endpoints, ALB). Two for PAID capacity in uat, three in prod. dev is single-AZ on purpose: synthetic data, and an AZ loss there is not an incident.
DISASTER RECOVERY — WHAT ACTUALLY EXISTS IN ap-south-2 (HYDERABAD)
R0 is WARM STANDBY. Active-active is explicitly not R0.
"Warm standby" is not something a platform team can provision from. This is the resource list. EVERYTHING BELOW IS ap-south-2 — nothing else is.
D1 · D2 · D3 · D6 · D7 are provisioned in the SAME change as their ap-south-1 primaries
Same module, DR parameters. No NAT until failover
without images, RTO is a build
S3 replica buckets: raw · docs · audit-archive
CRR + Object Lock 7 y ON THE REPLICA + lag alarm
Aurora DR — Global secondary OR Backup copy
Architecture fixes the outcome, not the option
PITR is same-region and is NOT a DR feature
data replicated without its key is not recoverable
a restored Aurora with no credential is not a service
NO — created at failover, or node groups at 0
This is what 'warm' means: data ready, compute unpaid
YES — the record IS the deliverable
declare, restore, verify, serve — wall-clock timed
Broken release rolled back, data intact, timed
NOT DR IN R0: a second running EKS cluster · active-active traffic · cross-region read routing · MSK MirrorMaker (there is no MSK) · a DR ElastiCache · any resource outside India (FF-08, control C6).

THE MONEY PATH IS NOT RESTORED, IT IS RECONCILED. Restoring the payment schema tells you what the platform believed; only reconciliation against the AU Bank PG tells you what actually happened. A DR exercise that passes without running reconciliation has not tested the payment path.
OUTSIDE — BANK SYSTEMS AND INSURANCE PROVIDERS ARE TWO DIFFERENT BOUNDARIES
architecture does not invent the bank network
NEEDS Direct Connect / VPN / bank proxy
DECISION HAS AN EXTERNAL LEAD TIME
WS-2 Phase 2 — do NOT block R0 on it
Keycloak-local users are fine in dev
callback on a separate allowlisted route
egress on the NAT Elastic IP, allowlisted
R0 POLLS — no inbound webhook exists
PROVISIONING SEQUENCE — WHAT IS NEEDED, IN WHAT ORDER, AND WHAT BREAKS IF IT IS LATE
R0-LLD.md §12.1 · no business service starts before P0–P3
Each band is gated on the one above it; within a band the order is free. P0–P3 are the S09 critical path — build wave W0 is 'no services: pipeline, IaC, environments'.
WHAT BREAKS IF IT IS LATE
Organizations + 5 accounts · region SCP · Terraform state + locking · security account · KMS CMK hierarchy · policy-as-code
Anything built before the region SCP must be re-verified by hand for S09-G9
VPC x 3 envs · 3 AZ subnet tiers · NAT + ELASTIC IPS · security groups · VPC endpoints · Route 53 private · ACM · flow logs
LONGEST EXTERNAL LEAD TIME — the EIP list must reach 1SB and the PG before UAT
EKS x 3 envs, private endpoint · node groups · add-ons · Kyverno/Gatekeeper admission · NetworkPolicy default-deny · Karpenter (thin)
Admission policy retro-fitted onto running workloads is a migration, not a control
ONE Aurora cluster + schemas + roles · DynamoDB + PITR · S3 + OBJECT LOCK · AWS Backup · ap-south-2 replication (D1-D3, D6, D7)
Object Lock CANNOT be applied retroactively — evidence written before it is outside the 7-year claim
Internal ALB · API Gateway · CloudFront + WAF + Shield · Route 53 public · SEPARATE IP-allowlisted PG-callback route
The PG-callback route is needed at W3, before the RM edge at W4 — treating 'the edge' as one item costs a wave
Keycloak on EKS + Aurora keycloak/identity schemas · Secrets Manager + rotation · IRSA per deployable · Secrets Store CSI
The PDP fails closed by design — no identity means nothing can be authorised. Not a 'later' item
CloudWatch with PII masking · AMP + AMG · X-Ray or ADOT · AUDIT PIPE SEPARATED from the operational pipe · dashboards + alert routing
Debugging the first end-to-end journey without correlated traces is where schedules are actually lost
ECR + immutable tags + scan on push · GitHub Actions to ECR · Argo CD · promote by digest · migration job in the deploy path
Rebuilding per environment breaks S09-E02-S02 and makes every UAT result unattributable
RESTORE executed and timed · ROLLBACK drill in UAT · secret rotation exercised · deletion refused on a locked object · residency enumerated
S09-G4/G7/G8/G9 accept RECORDS, not designs. None of this can be produced in gate week
WHAT EACH BUILD WAVE NEEDS TO ALREADY EXIST
+ NAT EIPs ALLOWLISTED BY 1SB · S3 raw locked
+ PG-callback route · settlement path · docs + audit-archive locked · D3 live
+ CloudFront + WAF + public API Gateway · internal ALB · SMS/email egress
THE TWO ITEMS WITH AN EXTERNAL LEAD TIME — START THESE FIRST
1. Publishing the NAT Elastic IP list to 1SilverBullet and to the AU Bank Payment Gateway for allowlisting.
Decide the NAT count BEFORE publishing — every EIP added afterwards is a second round-trip through someone else's change process.
2. The CBS and Bank AD connectivity pattern: Direct Connect, VPN, or a bank-hosted reverse proxy.
A joint Shivanshi + bank-network + Deepali decision, named as an S09 entry criterion. Until it exists, #4 Customer and WS-2 federation can only be stubbed, in dev.
Neither can be accelerated by working harder. Both depend on parties outside this programme.
DO NOT PROVISION IN R0 — every one of these is in the target-state review, and building it now is scope drift
architecture-review/04 is the North Star estate, not this request
the transactional outbox is the R0 async mechanism
in-process TTL cache; idempotency in the owning store
ADR-008 — one cluster, a schema per context
▸ Public ALB / public RDS / public EKS endpoint
only API Gateway is public — standing constraint
R0 is NetworkPolicy + IRSA + in-app timeouts and breakers
▸ Kong / Nginx Plus / F5 / any forward-proxy product
API Gateway + internal ALB is the whole proxy estate
#18 Reporting & MIS is S13 / R1 — the pilot funnel is not a warehouse
R0 polls (S-11) — do not open a public surface with no consumer
▸ Amazon Cognito as the R0 IdP
ARCH-018 — Keycloak first, behind a neutral adapter
▸ A PersistentVolumeClaim on any business service
state is Aurora / DynamoDB / S3; a PVC on Keycloak is an unreplicated identity SoR
AMP + AMG, so we do not own Prometheus volumes
▸ A customer-facing CloudFront distribution for DIY
▸ Render.com as an environment or a data path
ADR-001 — dev preview only, never PII, never a gate artefact
▸ Any resource outside ap-south-1, except DR replicas in ap-south-2
no colour appears on this page that is not on this row (HA-08)
LOB-partitioned shared — ONE deployment, behaviour resolved from configuration keyed by (lob, …); never a second copy and never an if (lob == …)
AZ matrix glyphs: ● required · ◐ conditional · ○ deliberately absent · — not AZ-bound
Containers say WHERE. Node fills say WHEN. That is the whole encoding.
